event: Elsie wakes to the bread smell and finds the honey-bun parcels by the door where she left them.
She reads her notebook: Tamsin, ankle, check it; Tilly, her father, clocks.

memory.fact: Elsie keeps a notebook of the birthdays and favourite things of people she loves.

event: She tells Mrs Pennywhistle they are going after a lost goat, and the fern takes it gravely.

memory.fact: Elsie's houseplants travel with her in a crate, and every one has a name.
The Underbloom is a dungeon beneath the old flower market.
The Underbloom is a dungeon beneath the old flower market.

event: She laces the halter, pins the clip, and packs the parcels, salve and bandages.

memory.fact: Elsie wears a cropped cream halter top laced up the front, a short sage-green skirt and tall boots.

event: Downstairs she gives the baker back her paper, folded, and the baker nods.
The guild hall is half empty this early, and the charcoal door stands open.
Cora is at the table inside with her ledger, writing, and looks up.

memory.fact: Cora's glossy black hair is pulled into a severe low bun, never a strand loose.
Cora carries a black leather ledger and writes everything down in a small, exact hand.

event: Elsie holds out the parcel with Cora written across it in her round hand.
Cora reads her own name on the paper a long moment before she takes it.
She puts it in her coat pocket unopened, and says the goat is in the afternoon.
Elsie says she knows, she only wanted Cora to have it while it was fresh.
Elsie waits on the bench by the quest board while the hall fills up.
A party of three walks past, sees her tag, and crosses to the other side of the hall.
Elsie hums, and reads the F-rank notices again to have something to do with her eyes.

memory.fact: Now and then Elsie hums without knowing it.
On the F-rank board today: a lost goat somewhere in the Underbloom's first floor, three lanterns.

event: Tamsin comes in at ten with her hair dry for once, limping only a little.

memory.fact: Tamsin's hair is a wild mass of copper curls, barely tied back.
Tamsin fights with a great axe she calls Margery.

event: Elsie sits her on the bench and props her bitten ankle across her own knees.
She unwinds the bandage; the bite is clean, and she puts on fresh salve.
Tamsin holds very still, looking at the rafters, and her ears go red to the tips.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 30 → 35 (Elsie tended her ankle across her knees)

event: Elsie gives her a honey bun; Tamsin eats it in two bites and says it's the best she's had.
Tilly comes in after, quiet, her braids done tight and her goggles down round her neck.
She takes her bun and thanks Elsie only once, and Elsie notices the once.
At the desk the clerk gives them the lost-goat notice for the Underbloom.
Cora comes out of the charcoal door when the clerk calls the party's name.
At the Tipsy Heron Elsie buys stew for the three of them, and Tilly pushes hers round.

changes.note: Three bowls of stew at four pips, for Elsie, Tamsin and Tilly: 112 → 100 pips

event: Elsie asks Tilly, quietly, what is wrong.
Tilly says she has been frightened of being underground since she was small.

memory.fact: Tilly is frightened of being underground, and has been since she was small.
Tilly is frightened of being underground, and has been since she was small.
Tilly is frightened of being underground, and has been since she was small.

event: She says she didn't say so before, because the guild wants three, and she wanted to be one.
Tamsin says she can wait at the top, and there's no shame in it.
Tilly says the licence needs three, and she is one of the three.

memory.fact: The guild licenses a party into a dungeon only if it has three or more registered adventurers.

event: Elsie says then Tilly holds her hand the whole way, and lets go only when she likes.
Tilly looks at the hand Elsie holds out across the table, and takes it.

changes.note: Bond: Tilly 20 → 25 (told her fear; took Elsie's offered hand)

event: Cora watches their hands, then the stew, and pays for her own bowl.
The old flower market is an iron-and-glass hall full of stalls and morning-cut flowers.

memory.fact: The old flower market is an iron-and-glass hall where sellers still set out stalls each morning.
The old flower market is an iron-and-glass hall where sellers still set out stalls each morning.

event: A flower seller with red eyes stops them and asks if they are the guild.
Her goat Clover, a white nanny, went down the stair after dropped flowers three days ago.

memory.fact: The lost goat is Clover, a white nanny goat belonging to a flower seller in the market above.

Clover went down the stair after a dropped bunch of flowers three days ago and has not come up.

event: Elsie promises to bring Clover up, and the seller holds her hand in both of hers.
In the middle of the market a dry fountain has a stone stair going down inside it.

memory.fact: The Underbloom is reached by a stone stair down from the dry fountain in the old flower market.
The Underbloom is reached by a stone stair down from the dry fountain in the old flower market.

event: A guild clerk at the stair head writes the party in, and Elsie pays him for the licence.

changes.note: One silver lantern for the party's stair licence: 100 → 90 pips

memory.fact: A guild clerk at the stair head licenses parties down, a lantern a party, and logs them in and out.
A guild clerk at the stair head licenses parties down, a lantern a party, and logs them in and out.

event: Tamsin says the first floor is safe for F-rank, and a locked gate bars the second.

memory.fact: The first floor is counted safe for F-rank, and a locked guild gate bars the stair to the second.
The first floor is counted safe for F-rank, and a locked guild gate bars the stair to the second.

event: Tilly takes Elsie's hand at the first step down, and grips it.
They go down into old brick cellars, and Tilly shuts her eyes.
The brick vaults are grown over with pale flowers that glow, and no lamp is needed.

memory.fact: The first floor is old brick cellars overgrown with pale flowers that glow, so it needs no lamp.
The first floor is old brick cellars overgrown with pale flowers that glow, so it needs no lamp.

pictured.coverAfter: But it was not dark. Elsie stood in the first cellar and looked up

event: Elsie says, oh, Tilly, look, and Tilly opens her eyes and does not shut them again.

memory.fact: The first floor is old brick cellars overgrown with pale flowers that glow, so it needs no lamp.

event: Bloom beetles the size of cats graze the flowers, slow and shining.
Tamsin says leave the beetles be, they nip only when handled; Tilly nearly steps on one.

memory.fact: Bloom beetles the size of a cat graze the first floor's flowers, and nip only when handled.
Bloom beetles the size of a cat graze the first floor's flowers, and nip only when handled.

event: Elsie calls Clover's name down the long vault, and far off something bleats.
Tamsin warns them off the side passages, where stranglevine holds whatever brushes it.
On a stair landing Cora takes the honey bun out of her pocket and eats it, looking away.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 5 → 10 (kept the bun with her name, ate it on the stair)

memory.fact: Cora kept Elsie's honey bun in her pocket and ate it on the Underbloom stair.
Cora kept Elsie's honey bun in her pocket and ate it on the Underbloom stair.

event: Elsie sees it, and hums the whole length of the next vault.

memory.fact: Now and then Elsie hums without knowing it.

event: Tilly's grip on her hand loosens a little, and then a little more.
The bleating leads them to the heart of the floor, to an old cistern room.

pictured.coverAfter: The bleating got louder as they went, closer and crosser, and led them in,

event: Stranglevine has grown across the doorway in a thick green web.

memory.fact: Stranglevine has grown across the cistern room's doorway since Clover went in.
Stranglevine has grown across the cistern room's doorway since Clover went in.
Stranglevine has grown across the cistern room's doorway since Clover went in.

event: Inside, a white goat stands in the glowing flowers, eating, and glows faintly herself.

memory.fact: Clover is in the old cistern room at the first floor's heart, eating the glowing flowers.
Clover is in the old cistern room at the first floor's heart, eating the glowing flowers.
Clover is in the old cistern room at the first floor's heart, eating the glowing flowers.

event: Elsie laughs out loud: Clover has eaten so many flowers she has lit up.
Elsie reaches through a gap toward Clover, and the vine closes on her wrist.
A second strand wraps her ankle and pulls; Elsie is held fast against the web.
Tamsin lifts Margery, then stops: the vine is wound too close round Elsie to swing.
Cora takes hold of the strand at Elsie's wrist with both gloved hands, and it holds.
Tamsin says it holds until it is cut or burnt.

memory.fact: Stranglevine grows over the side passages and holds whatever brushes it until it is cut or burnt.
Stranglevine grows over the side passages and holds whatever brushes it until it is cut or burnt.

event: Tilly lets go of Elsie at last and pulls two vials off her belt with shaking hands.
She pours one into the other, and a small blue flame stands up in the glass.
Her hands go steady; she holds the flame to the vine a finger from Elsie's skin.
The vine at Elsie's wrist blackens and lets go, then the strand at her ankle.
Tilly stares at the little flame in her own hand as if someone else had made it.
Elsie hugs her hard and says she is a genius, an actual genius, and she loves her.
Tilly goes pink from her collar to her hair, and holds the flame out of the way.
Tamsin cuts the rest of the web down with Margery in three clean strokes.
Clover trots out glowing and eats a flower out of Elsie's hand.
Elsie knots a bandage through Clover's collar for a lead, and the goat follows her.
Cora opens the ledger by the cistern door and writes more than one line this time.
She closes it before Elsie can ask, and walks ahead of them toward the stair.
They come up out of the fountain into the market with a glowing goat.
The clerk at the stair head writes them out, and stares at the goat.
The flower seller drops her shears and runs, and kneels with her arms round Clover.
She signs the notice on her knee, crying, and gives each of them a flower.
Tilly puts hers behind her ear, the way Elsie wears her clip.
At the guild hall the clerk counts out the goat pay; Elsie, Tamsin and Tilly each pocket a third.
Cora says the hall's business with them is done today, and goes to the charcoal door.
The three of them sit on the canal wall outside with their boots over the water.
Tilly says she was frightened the whole time; Elsie says she knows, and Tilly was brave.
Tilly falls asleep against Elsie's shoulder with the flower still behind her ear.
Tamsin watches the two of them, and says, low, that this is new to her.
Elsie asks what is new; Tamsin looks at the water and says, people who wait for her.
At dusk the lamplighters' boats come by, and Tilly wakes up mortified.
They part at the bridge, and Tilly hugs Elsie before she runs.
In the attic Elsie puts the market flower in a cup by the plants.
In the notebook she writes: Tilly, underground, hold her hand; she makes fire.
Under Tamsin she writes: her mother likes honey cake.
Under Cora she writes: ate the bun on the stair, and wrote more than one line.
